title: Connections and the tests that may reach them
description: What connection-paths found in a module's source: each place the code opens or uses a connection to something outside the program, each test that may reach one with a chain of calls showing how, and what it could not resolve or chose not to follow. Written by connection-paths and read by the connection-list skill; 'may' means measurement confirms or clears each test.

kind.description: The kind of connection, from connection-paths' rules. A url may be a file or jar as well as a remote server.

method.description: A method as type#name(parameter types), the types as simple names without generics; constructors are <init>, a type's field initialisers <fields>.

address.description: Where a connection's address comes from, as far as the source shows.

value.description: The literal ({?} for parts that can't be known), the setting's, variable's or JNDI name, 'x of method' for a parameter, or the code that builds it.

via.description: For a setting: the method that reads it, or @Value.

setting_value.description: For a setting: its value in the repo's settings files.

placeholder.description: The setting's value looks like a placeholder for a person to fill in.

schema.description: Version 2 adds each point's address and whether it stays local, the systems, and each test's systems; version 3 adds the tests that start a framework. Nothing is ever removed.

tests_starting_a_framework.description: Version 3: how many tests start a framework.

call.description: The rule the call matched, as type#method, or @ and an annotation's full name for a client that is only an annotated interface (Feign, Retrofit, Spring @HttpExchange, MicroProfile @RegisterRestClient), whose address is the annotation's url or base URI.

local.description: Present only when the point stays on this machine: the reason, such as an in-memory or file database, a classpath resource, or a parameter no code passes.

systems.description: The systems the connection points make: by host, else by setting, variable or JNDI name, else by the class that opens them. Local, host-lookup and process points belong to none.

alternatives.description: Other systems whose points override the same interface or superclass method: alternatives a program picks between, for a person to say whether they are one.

shared_chain.description: Calls every test reaching it goes through, nearest the test first: the seam where one stand-in covers them all.

tests.description: Only the tests that may reach a connection; the key matches testing/tests.yaml's: the fully qualified class, a dot, the method.

through_set_up.description: True when the chain goes through the test's set-up methods or fields, not its own body.

chain.description: From the test to the connection point, one method a step.

systems.description: Version 2: the systems the test may reach, by name.

tests_starting_a_framework.description: Version 3: the tests whose class, a superclass in the source, or the class around a @Nested one starts a framework (Spring, Testcontainers, Quarkus, Micronaut, Arquillian) by annotation. Starting one may open connections whatever the test's body does. A test can be here and in tests.

test.description: The same key as in tests: the fully qualified class, a dot, the method.

framework.description: The annotation as written, such as @SpringBootTest, @Testcontainers or @RunWith(SpringJUnit4ClassRunner.class).

annotated_on.description: The class carrying the annotation: the test's own, a superclass in the source, or a class around a @Nested one.

not_resolved.description: Calls the symbol solver could not resolve, by reason, most common first; a missing library shows as its types' names.

example.description: The first place it was seen, as file:line and the message.

dispatch_points_not_followed.description: Calls through an interface or superclass with more overriding methods than the limit, reported instead of followed.
